To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energetics of atmospheres implicated clusters of sulfuric acid and ammonia can be accurately calculated by the PW6B95 density-functional theory method with the MG3s basis set, and the inclusion of the dispersion correction is essential for the calculation of accurate binding energies.

(1) the binding energy of a sulfuric acid dimer to a dimethylamine molecule is about 1 kcal/mol, which is significantly smaller than the binding energy to an ammonia molecule, and that (2) the binding energies for the formation of clusters containing sulfuric acid, dimethylamine, and ammonia molecules are in the 1-2 kcal/mol range, which is comparable to the binding energy of an ammonia molecule to an ammonium sulfate cluster.

(1) the binding energy per sulfur atom of the (H2SO4)x(SNH3)y(DMA)m clusters decreases with increasing cluster size, (2) the binding energy is larger for clusters that contain more DMA, (3) the binding energy of the DMA molecules increases with the cluster size, and (4) the binding energy decreases as DMA replaces sulfuric acid in the cluster.
